A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GoRank/GoTrim research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison; no material reading gaps remain.

before.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4.3 and Appendices G–H report original simulations, Basel temperature-data experiments, and asynchronous-ranking comparisons.

after.justification: v7 retains original empirical results and adds larger-network, clustered-network, and sparse-graph experiments in Appendices I–K.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–6 retain their procedures, including the already-present asynchronous variant. Appendix L newly outlines a multivariate adaptation that ranks observation norms, discards the largest floor(alpha*n) observations, and averages the remainder. This is a proposed extension, not an evaluated replacement.

E1.justification: The synthetic ranking and contaminated-mean tasks and Basel Luftklima data remain. Appendices J–K add weakly connected clusters, cycle graphs, and 3-regular graphs as evaluation environments. Probabilistic network failures and multivariate data are discussed without demonstrated empirical coverage.

E2.justification: Matched ranking comparisons retain Baseline and Baseline++; trimmed-mean comparisons retain GoTrim with alternative ranking, ClippedGossip, and the corrupted-mean reference. The new related-work table does not establish additional empirical baselines.

E3.justification: The retained main experiments keep their settings and metrics. Appendix I adds 1,000- and 5,000-node experiments with longer iteration horizons, while Appendix K specifies 150,000 iterations for sparse-graph tests. These are additional protocols, not revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Appendices I–K substantially expand scalability and connectivity stress analyses through larger networks, weak inter-cluster links, and contrasting sparse topologies. Appendix L additionally reports limited benefits from optimized sampling. Conversely, v6 Figure 6's cross-graph weight-error analysis is removed, although the main Figure 3(a) analysis remains.

E5.justification: Both retain 1,000 trials for Figure 2(a) and mean/standard-deviation reporting over 100 trials for Figures 2(b–c). No new seed-reporting, confidence-interval, significance-testing, or repeated-run reporting procedure is specified.

E6.justification: Figures 8–10 and Appendix J add substantial scaling and topology results, including GoRank errors below 0.1 on larger networks. Figure 3(a)'s empirical weight-error profile changes, and v6 Figure 6's results disappear. A new inconsistency matters: Figure 9(b) shows GoTrim + Baseline++ converging well on the 1,000-node grid, contrary to Appendix I's description.

T1.justification: Appendix J introduces a failure-model derivation using a weighted Laplacian and effective connectivity c/2 under 50% edge failures. The principal convergence and breakdown proofs remain substantively unchanged. The mean-square bound newly included in Theorem 2 was already established in v6 Lemma C.1.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contribution bullets retain their claims. Section 5 explicitly identifies Byzantine robustness as future work and strengthens the applicability statement to natural extensions involving rank statistics and the Winsorized mean; v6 presented extensions as future directions with precision difficulties.

C2.justification: v7 substantially expands discussion of honest-node assumptions, connectivity versus sparsity, network disruptions, asynchronous analysis, and multivariate extensions. Appendix L adds tightness and near-optimality assertions despite acknowledging missing lower bounds. The earlier explicit limitation concerning accurate median/Winsorized-mean estimation is removed.

D1.justification: New graph-construction details include three clusters with five connecting edges and sparse-graph edge counts. Appendix G.1 adds a runtime qualification excluding large-scale experiments. Hardware, Basel preprocessing, and statements about supplementary code/data availability remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v7 adds the sensor-outlier survey and optimized-mixing references, removes Hastings (1970) and Xiao et al. (2006), and adds a comparison table covering decentralization, unbiasedness, and convergence rates. This expands research positioning without changing the evaluated baseline set.

P1.justification: Targeted revisions expand the sensor motivation and remarks, restructure Section 5 into named discussion topics, and rewrite the former Appendix I as Appendix L. Most technical exposition remains matched; several changes simply shorten notation.

P2.justification: v7 adds a method-comparison table and three multipanel figures covering scaling and sparse graphs, while removing v6 Figure 6. The former Figures 7–8 survive as Figures 6–7. Figure 3(a) is replotted with a revised vertical scale, and several existing displays move.

improvement.justification: The added stress tests and honest-node clarification strengthen evidence and scope documentation. However, Figure 9(b) contradicts Appendix I's Baseline++ interpretation, the new comparison table conflicts with Appendix A about decentralization, and Appendix L asserts near-optimality without lower bounds. These substantive reliability issues leave the net quality effect uncertain.
